newsitem.title: INDIA: Simple majority needed to win India vote.
newsitem.headline: Simple majority needed to win India vote.

text.p: A vote of confidence in Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government, to be taken on Friday, will pass if it gets a simple majority of legislators present and voting.
The parliamentary session for the test of strength is scheduled to begin at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT), and will be followed by a debate and voting, for which no time has yet been fixed.
The 545-seat lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, currently has 542 members. Two seats are vacant and one is occupied by the speaker, P.A. Sangma, who can vote in the event of a tie.
General elections in April and May last year yielded a hung parliament.
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is the biggest single party with 162 deputies. With its four allies, the BJP controls 193 votes -- well shy of an absolute majority.

Deve Gowda's 15-party United Front coalition controls 180 votes. Its strongest component is the prime minister's centrist Janata Dal party with 45 legislators, followed by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) with 32.
Deve Gowda has been propped up by the Congress party, which controls 140 votes but withdrew its backing on March 30.
Deve Gowda proposed the vote of confidence after President Shankar Dayal Sharma asked him to prove his majority in parliament.
A quorum of at least 55 members of parliament would have to be present for the vote of confidence to be taken, a parliament spokesman said.
The BJP held power for 12 days in May but quit when it failed to muster enough support to win a vote of confidence.
